LESSON: VIRTUES: ISLAMIC CLOTHING AND ADORNMENT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq
Topic 5.2: Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment, part of Akhlaq in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why should a Muslim observe the Islamic clothing and adornment? 2. How can the Muslim youth promote Islamic identity through dress?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the rules and regulations governing dressing and adornment in Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assess the rationale for the Islamic code of dressing and adornment as a basis for safeguarding modesty,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. practise the Islamic code of dressing and adornment in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the Islamic code of dress as an act of ibaadah.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the rules and regulations governing dressing and adornment in Islam,

   Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. assess the rationale for the Islamic code of dressing and adornment as a basis for safeguarding modesty,

   Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. practise the Islamic code of dressing and adornment in day-to-day life,

   Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the Islamic code of dress as an act of ibaadah.

   Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or on available reference materials the rules and regulations governing dressing and adornment (tattoing,beautification surgery, wigs) in Islam and present in class,

2. distinguish between male and female code of dress and adornment, make charts and display,

3. brainstorm on the purpose of dressing and adornment in Islam and make notes,

4. search online or on available reference materials the rationale 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or on available reference materials the rules and regulations governing dressing and adornment (tattoing,beautification surgery, wigs) in Islam and present in class,
2. distinguish between male and female code of dress and adornment, make charts and display,
3. brainstorm on the purpose of dressing and adornment in Islam and make notes,
4. search online or on available reference materials the rationale 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
